scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements for the 4-m telescopic levelling staff, which is a mechanical device used in tertiary levelling to provide height control for topographical or engineering surveys [1, 2].

requirements.detail: The staff must consist of three distinct sliding sections. Design tolerances must ensure the top section slides smoothly into the middle section, and the middle section slides into the bottom section [1].

The staff must be manufactured from one of the following approved seasoned timbers: Teak (Tectona grandis Linn. f.), Cypress (Cupressus torulosa Don.), Kail (Pinus wallichiana A.B. Jacks.), Deodar (Cedrus deodara Loudon), Aini (Artocarpus hirsuta Lamk.), Champ (Michelia sp.), or Hollock (Terminalia myriocarpa) [3].

The selected timber must be thoroughly seasoned, radially sawn, and completely free from physical defects like knots, cracks, shakes, insect attack, and decay. The moisture content must be strictly maintained within the range of 8 to 12 percent [3].
The nomenclature, dimensions, and profiles of different assembly parts (including the shoe, bottom cap, middle cap, and top) must conform precisely to Figures 1 to 9 of the standard [2].
Any observed or calculated test value expressing the result of a test must be rounded off to the same number of significant places as the specified value, in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 [2].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11961 : 1986 is the national Indian Standard specification governing 4-metre telescopic levelling staves used as height control mechanical devices in tertiary topographical or engineering surveys [1]. It specifies a three-section sliding assembly designed to slide compactly into one another [1]. To prevent environmental distortion and ensure long-term measuring accuracy, the standard restricts manufacture to seven approved, high-grade seasoned timbers (including Teak, Deodar, and Cypress) that must be radially sawn with a strictly monitored moisture range of 8 to 12 percent [3]. It defines exact part geometries for the shoe, caps, and top through figures, and leverages IS 2 : 1960 for rounding compliance values [2].
